---
name: memory
description: Using the multimodal memory this run keeps for you -- the log, the episodes with their frames, the earlier lives, your own files -- and the workshop turn at the start of a life.
---

# Memory

You do not build a memory here; you USE one. The harness records everything (immutable,
grep-able) and keeps what you write under `mine/` (yours, carried to your next life).

## What is recorded, and how to ask it

- `logs.txt`: every turn -- `[STATE]` position/pitch/yaw, `[EVENT]` what broke, dropped,
  was crafted or picked up, `[NOTE]` what the runner and your procedures observed,
  `[INV]` inventory changes, `[PLAN]` your own briefings. `grep -n` is the query.
- `episodes/ep_NNNNNN/`: one per plan entry, with `observation/image.png` (the view the
  entry started from), `state/state.json`, `action.json`, `outcome.json` (moved,
  descended, inventory delta, events, tags such as `stuck`, `damage`, `milestone`).
  `./tools/episodes.py --last 5 | --steps A B | --near X Z [--radius R] | --tag damage
  | --action go_to | --grep text`; add `--sheet out.png` to tile the frames of the
  matches into one image, `--json` for rows; `--then-now <id> --q "<question>"` writes
  that episode's frame beside the current view as `then_now.png` -- the recognition
  check before you walk to a remembered place, or on arrival. Pass `--q` on every
  look: the record keeps what the look was for.
- Frames are files: `./tools/zoom.py <frame.png> x y w h [out.png]` magnifies a region
  4x for `view_image`; a script with numpy/PIL can read many frames and answer one
  question over all of them (where the orange was; which frames show a screen).
- `previous/life_<i>/`: the complete records of earlier lives in this same world
  (same seed, same spawn), oldest first, each with its logs.txt, episodes, index and
  `mine/` (its notes, guide and scripts). `./tools/episodes.py --previous ...` queries
  them all; `grep -n 'LAVA AHEAD\|YOU DIED\|obsidian' previous/life_*/logs.txt` is the
  fastest map of what they found and what killed them. The world resets between lives:
  terrain, water, lava and ore are where they were; nothing built or dropped survives;
  their step numbers are theirs.
- `mine/`: yours. `mine/notes.md` (what worked, what each script assumes),
  `mine/GUIDE.md` (what you took from the earlier lives), `mine/procedures/`,
  `mine/reflexes/`, any data or images you save. Carried whole to your next life.

## The workshop turn

The first turn of a life with `previous/` is a WORKSHOP, not a play turn: read the
lives' guides, notes and death lines, run the query tool over them, write or update
`mine/GUIDE.md` (verified places with coordinates, the life/step they come from and
the episode id whose frame shows the place, what each life died of and where, which scripts and reflexes earned their keep and
which assumptions broke), read the scripts installed for you in `mine/` ([INSTALLED] in the contract),
keep, fix or retire each, and only then plan. One no-op plan is a fine end to a workshop turn:
turns cost wall clock, not game steps.

## When to look at a frame

`view_image <png>` opens any frame: an episode's `observation/image.png`, an earlier
life's under `previous/`, a sheet from `--sheet`, a crop from `tools/zoom.py`, the pair
from `--then-now`. Write the question first ("is the lava in the next cell or two cells
off?", "is this the ledge I poured from?") and pass it as `--q`. The `[STATE]`/`[NOTE]`
numbers say WHERE and THAT; the frame says WHAT -- one look costs one image. Open frames
before you walk to a remembered place and on arrival (`--then-now`), after a hit (the
frame at the hit shows what hit you), when `OBSERVED vs EXPECTED` disagree (the entry's
frame is cited beside the outcome), before a route across ground you have not walked,
and when a plan failed twice for a reason you cannot name. The 22 runs before this one
opened an earlier episode's frame 32 times in 850,000 steps and an earlier life's 3
times; every one of those looks was after a stall, none before a walk.

## Working memory

`mine/working.md` is put in front of you every turn as `[WORKING]` and survives a
context reset: the plan you are on and why, its next visible prediction, the
contradictions you have not resolved, the entries and frames you would re-open (paths).
Rewrite it when the plan changes, under 40 lines. `mine/GUIDE.md`
is what is true of this world across lives; `working.md` is what you are doing now.

## Death forensics

After `YOU DIED`, before you rebuild anything: `./tools/episodes.py --steps <death-60>
<death> --sheet death.png --q "what killed me"`, view it, and write one line into
`mine/GUIDE.md`: step, place, cause, what you will refuse next time.
The frame tells a burn from a mob: flames over the lower view, orange at the feet. Of
the 20 deaths in the earlier runs, 11 were lava or fire, 5 a mob, and 3 happened within
5 blocks of a place the same life had already written down as lava or a death --
recorded, and never turned into a refusal. `skills/memory/scripts/death_sheet.py` does
the tiling for the last death in the log.

## Record every firing and every death

A reflex that fired, a fall, a hit, a death: one line in `mine/notes.md` with the step,
the place, the cause and what you changed. That line is what your next life reads
first. `skills/memory/scripts/where_was.py <keyword> [--previous]` is an example of a
memory query written as a script.

The built-in set is the ATOMS (closed-loop aims and walks, the GUI cursor, one-call
craft, placements, the bucket, watch/pillar/eat/throw). Everything task-shaped you build
yourself as `mine/procedures/<name>.py` (the script contract is in the main contract).
This file says what a good one looks like.

anything you write there survives the turn and is carried to your next life under
`previous/life_<i>/mine/`. A script at `mine/procedures/<name>.py` is a procedure from the
next turn on: call it as `{"procedure": "<name>", "args": {...}}` like a built-in. The
contract of such a script:
- the harness runs `python mine/procedures/<name>.py --args '<json of args>'` with the
  state on STDIN as JSON: `{"step", "max_steps", "pos": {"x","y","z","pitch","yaw"},
  "health", "food", "inventory": {item: count}, "hotbar": [{"slot","item","n"}],
  "gui_open", "dimension"}`;
- it prints ONE plan to stdout in exactly the actions.json shape,
  `{"actions": [{"procedure": ..., "args": {...}}, {"action": {...}, "repeat": N}]}`,
  built from the built-in procedures and raw actions (never another own procedure); the
  plan goes through the same caps and checks as yours;
- the first line of its docstring is its index entry, an optional `PARAMS = {"n": "how
  many"}` dict names its arguments; the `[OWN]` block of every turn lists your scripts
  with their call counts, or says why one cannot be called;
- a script that fails (non-zero exit, 10 s timeout, no JSON) costs one [NOTE] with the
  last error line and runs nothing; the rest of your plan still runs;
- it may read `logs.txt`, `grid.jsonl`, `episodes/` (`tools/episodes.py`) and your own
  `mine/` files to decide what to emit -- it sees the same numbers you do.
Write a procedure only after the same sequence has worked TWICE by hand, then call it by
name from then on; a script you never call again was a turn spent on nothing. Keep your
notes in `mine/notes.md` (what worked, coordinates, what each script assumes).

**Working memory.** `mine/working.md` is yours and is put in front of you every turn
as `[WORKING]`: the plan you are on and why, its next visible prediction, the
contradictions you have not resolved, and the entries or frames you would re-open
(paths). It survives a context reset, so the turn after one starts from it instead of
from the log. Rewrite it when the plan changes, not every turn; keep it under 40
lines. `mine/GUIDE.md` is what is true of this world across
lives; `working.md` is what you are doing now.

**Your own reflexes.** A script at `mine/reflexes/<name>.py` is a REFLEX: the harness
runs it every 4 ticks WHILE YOUR PLAN EXECUTES (never inside a screen, never while the
runner's own escape is running), with the same STDIN state as a procedure plus
`lava_frac` (the share of the lower view that is lava, 0-1), `fire_frac` (the share
that is flame-coloured: a fire block or the burning overlay reads 5-15x `lava_frac`, a
lake 0.3-0.5x, the overlay over a pool 1.5-2.5x and a pool one block away 1.0-1.3x),
`hurt_100` (the health lost in the last 100 ticks, healing not counted: flames on screen
and `hurt_100` >= 1 is a burn), `in_lava` (true when your head is under lava: the view
is then a flat red that reads as neither of the two), `mainhand` (the item held), `health_prev` and
`pos_prev` (4 ticks ago), `entry` (the plan entry running: a procedure name or "raw"),
`atom` (inside one of your own procedures, the built-in or raw step it is running now;
otherwise the same as `entry`), `queue_len` and `runner_reflex`. It prints NOTHING (or `{}`) to stay quiet, and to
fire, ONE JSON object `{"stop": true, "note": "<why, one line>", "actions": [...]}`:
`stop` drops the rest of your plan, `note` reaches your next turn as `[REFLEX <name>]
...`, `actions` (optional: built-in procedures and raw actions, at most 6 entries and
120 ticks, never an own procedure) run at once through the same caps and checks. A
reflex that fired stays quiet for 40 ticks; one that fails (non-zero exit, 3 s
timeout, bad JSON) three times in a row is switched off until you edit it; at most 4

import json
import sys

PARAMS = {"yaw": "cardinal tunnel heading", "steps": "one to three columns (129 ticks each)"}

actions = []

way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:

  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --

  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.

GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:

2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.

   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)

hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives

container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is

**Survival** (a previous run died twice and lost everything):
- **What kills runs: monsters in unlit tunnels, drops into caves and ravines, lava met
  while moving, and in the Nether every ledge into the lava sea.** Monsters are reported
  on no channel; the health drop is the only warning, and a plan standing still under
  hits (digging, sweeping, clicking) is how most deaths began. In THIS run the runner
  does not act for you: no stop at lava, no pillar or bunker on a hit, no swim-up, no
  refusal of a repeated plan. Your reflexes under `mine/reflexes/` are the tick layer
  (`skills/reflexes/SKILL.md`), and your plans carry the doctrine: torches and a 1x2
  tunnel with its ceiling intact; a sword in the hotbar before going deep and food in
  the inventory (no natural healing below 18 food); descend by stairs, never by jumping
  into a hole; back away from orange and seal it with a block; break a skeleton's line
  of sight instead of charging it; an **enderman** that you look in the eye from under 4 blocks teleports away, so once one is close keep the crosshair on its body or legs, never on its head; in the Nether sneak, never sprint or jump while
  moving, dig the way down, bridge over lava. Verify ARRIVAL at a remembered place
  against the live position readout before drawing conclusions about the site.
- **Obsidian is lake work, and a death there costs the chain its tools.** Obsidian breaks
  only under a DIAMOND pickaxe (any other tool breaks it with no drop) and lies where
  water met lava, so the pool is beside every cell: a mined cell is a HOLE over it --
  never step on or across one, fill it with cobblestone, and take the drop from the edge.
  Before the lake, leave the spare diamonds, the flint and steel and any second pickaxe in
  a chest at the base: what you carry burns when you die there, and without a diamond
  pickaxe the chain is back at the diamonds. Where a sheet cannot be mined safely, water
  poured onto a lava SOURCE casts obsidian in place. Your reflexes are quiet while a
  screen is open: at the lake never pour, craft or sort from the inventory screen -- a
  life at 8 health did, took the lava's 4 with the screen up, and died pillaring at 4.
  A bed (3 wool from sheep + 3 planks;
  `use_at` it at night) skips the night and moves your respawn to it -- set one by the
  work site before the lake and the portal, so a death costs a walk of ten blocks, not
  two hundred, and the drops are still there.
- **A death at night is followed by another.** You respawn at the world spawn, at the
  surface, with nothing, and what killed you is still out there: of 33 deaths in four
  lives, 18 were at the surface and 22 were mobs, seven in a row in one night. After a
  respawn in the dark, dig two blocks down where you stand (or wall yourself in with
  anything) BEFORE a single step, and walk only in daylight; the drops wait ~6,000
  ticks, the night is 12,000. The bed is the first thing to make once you have seen a
  sheep -- no life of the record ever made one.
- A big health drop interrupts your plan with a [NOTE]; find the danger before resuming.
- If you die, the harness [NOTE] gives the death coordinates. Your items despawn there
  after ~6000 ticks: recover by stairs (never jump into a shaft) or rebuild -- decide by
  what is cheaper, and write the decision into your plan.

**Movement**:
- **Turn, then move.** A yaw change and "forward" in the same tick curve your path into an

- `moved=0.00` repeatedly in [STATE] means you are blocked by terrain, not standing still

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every

whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a

pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a

  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --

1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

/usr/bin/id: cannot find name for group ID 5142
**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

[A screen must be open. Name the occupied cells from [GRID]. Furnace slots never need this -- a furnace keeps its in/fuel/out contents when the screen closes.]
14:- `cursor_to_cell(grid=<2x2, 3x3 or furnace>, cell=<row-major index (furnace: 0=smelt input, 1=fuel), or "out">)` -- Land the cursor ON a crafting or furnace cell (or the output). Closed loop, like cursor_to_slot.  [The named grid's screen must be the one that is open.]

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a

  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

"""aim_speckles: turn the crosshair onto the (x, y) pixel a 'mining stopped: ...-ore-like speckles' [NOTE] names, then mine that block and sweep its drop."""
# Example procedure (harness-written; copy it to mine/procedures/ and make it yours).
# Why it exists: the life that found the diamond did exactly this within 20 steps of the
# watcher's [NOTE] -- aim at the speckles, mine the block under the crosshair, walk to the
# drop. Lives that answered a sighting with "finish the column first" or "craft a sword
# first" never mined the ore at all: by the next turn the view had moved and the speckles
# were gone. So: a sighting [NOTE] outranks everything; call this from its (x, y) BEFORE any
# other look or step, while the view is still the flag-time view (the runner dropped the
# rest of the plan for exactly that).
# The frame the watcher reads is 640x360 with a 70-degree vertical field of view: the focal
# length is 180 / tan(35 deg) = 257 px, so an offset of d pixels from the centre (320, 180) is
# atan(d / 257) degrees -- 104 px right is 22 degrees of yaw, not the 17 a linear scale gives.
# Two 30-tick holds: ore takes longer than stone, and the hold is cut the moment the block
# breaks anyway. collect_drops then sweeps the drop; the milestone is the PICKUP, not the break.
import json, math, sys
PARAMS = {"x": "screen x from the [NOTE] (0-640)", "y": "screen y from the [NOTE] (0-360)",
          "pick": "hotbar slot 1-9 with the pickaxe (default: the best in the hotbar)"}
args = json.loads(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--args") + 1]) if "--args" in sys.argv else {}
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
if s.get("gui_open"):
    raise SystemExit("a screen is open: close_inventory first")
if "x" not in args or "y" not in args:
    raise SystemExit("pass x and y: the pixel the sighting [NOTE] names, e.g. (424, 145)")
x, y = float(args["x"]), float(args["y"])
if not (0 <= x <= 640 and 0 <= y <= 360):
    raise SystemExit("x must be 0-640 and y 0-360 (the [NOTE]'s frame)")
rank = {"diamond_pickaxe": 0, "iron_pickaxe": 1, "stone_pickaxe": 2, "wooden_pickaxe": 3}
picks = [h for h in s["hotbar"] if h.get("item") in rank]
if args.get("pick") is not None:
    picks = [h for h in picks if int(h["slot"]) + 1 == int(args["pick"])]
if not picks:
    raise SystemExit("no pickaxe in the hotbar (diamond ore needs IRON or better to drop a diamond)")
pick = min(picks, key=lambda h: rank[h["item"]])
F = 180.0 / math.tan(math.radians(35.0))               # 257 px
dpitch = round(math.degrees(math.atan((y - 180.0) / F)), 1)   # + is down, like the screen
dyaw = round(math.degrees(math.atan((x - 320.0) / F)), 1)     # + is right, like the screen
plan = [{"procedure": "equip_hotbar", "args": {"slot": int(pick["slot"]) + 1}},
        {"action": {"camera": [dpitch, dyaw]}, "repeat": 1},
        {"action": {"attack": 1}, "repeat": 30},
        {"action": {"attack": 1}, "repeat": 30},
        {"procedure": "collect_drops", "args": {"ticks": 48}}]
print(json.dumps({"actions": plan}))
