**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

  while moving, and in the Nether every ledge into the lava sea.** Monsters are reported

  against the live position readout before drawing conclusions about the site.

  only under a DIAMOND pickaxe (any other tool breaks it with no drop) and lies where
  water met lava, so the pool is beside every cell: a mined cell is a HOLE over it --
  never step on or across one, fill it with cobblestone, and take the drop from the edge.
  Before the lake, leave the spare diamonds, the flint and steel and any second pickaxe in
  a chest at the base: what you carry burns when you die there, and without a diamond
  pickaxe the chain is back at the diamonds. Where a sheet cannot be mined safely, water

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

contradictions you have not resolved, and the entries or frames you would re-open
(paths). It survives a context reset, so the turn after one starts from it instead of
from the log. Rewrite it when the plan changes, not every turn; keep it under 40
lines. `mine/GUIDE.md` is what is true of this world across
lives; `working.md` is what you are doing now.

**Your own reflexes.** A script at `mine/reflexes/<name>.py` is a REFLEX: the harness
runs it every 4 ticks WHILE YOUR PLAN EXECUTES (never inside a screen, never while the
runner's own escape is running), with the same STDIN state as a procedure plus
`lava_frac` (the share of the lower view that is lava, 0-1), `fire_frac` (the share
that is flame-coloured: a fire block or the burning overlay reads 5-15x `lava_frac`, a
lake 0.3-0.5x, the overlay over a pool 1.5-2.5x and a pool one block away 1.0-1.3x),
`hurt_100` (the health lost in the last 100 ticks, healing not counted: flames on screen
and `hurt_100` >= 1 is a burn), `in_lava` (true when your head is under lava: the view
is then a flat red that reads as neither of the two), `mainhand` (the item held), `health_prev` and
`pos_prev` (4 ticks ago), `entry` (the plan entry running: a procedure name or "raw"),
`atom` (inside one of your own procedures, the built-in or raw step it is running now;
otherwise the same as `entry`), `queue_len` and `runner_reflex`. It prints NOTHING (or `{}`) to stay quiet, and to
fire, ONE JSON object `{"stop": true, "note": "<why, one line>", "actions": [...]}`:
`stop` drops the rest of your plan, `note` reaches your next turn as `[REFLEX <name>]
...`, `actions` (optional: built-in procedures and raw actions, at most 6 entries and
120 ticks, never an own procedure) run at once through the same caps and checks. A
reflex that fired stays quiet for 40 ticks; one that fails (non-zero exit, 3 s
timeout, bad JSON) three times in a row is switched off until you edit it; at most 4
run, alphabetical; keep each under 50 ms -- read the state, not the logs. Reflexes
worth writing FIRST, from what killed earlier runs: lava coming into the lower view
while you walk or dig (stop, step back); a drop of 4+ blocks within a few ticks (stop,
look before moving); health falling with no lava in view (a mob -- stop a dig or a
sweep, pillar up or wall off); in the Nether, any walk with lava in view. The runner's guards are OFF in this run: your reflexes are the only tick layer.

**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

/usr/bin/id: cannot find name for group ID 5142
**Crafting is ONE call.** This engine has no craft command, so a recipe is performed the
way a human does it -- a screen, a cursor, clicks -- and the harness does that for you:
- `craft(item=..., count=1)` lays out the whole recipe from your REAL inventory (lifts
  each ingredient stack, right-clicks one item into every cell, puts the remainder back,
  takes the output, banks it -- tools go to the hotbar) and VERIFIES it on the
  `craft_item` statistic: its [NOTE] reads "+1 stone_pickaxe crafted ... hotbar 3" or
  says why nothing happened. The RIGHT screen must be open first: `open_inventory` for a
  2x2 recipe, a crafting table's screen for a 3x3 one. Several crafts fit one plan --
  `open_inventory, craft(planks, count=2), craft(stick), craft(crafting_table),
  close_inventory` is the whole wooden phase once the logs are in.
- `place_and_open(item="crafting_table")` (or `"furnace"`) puts the carried block on the
  ground one block ahead and opens its screen, moving it into the hotbar first when
  needed. Face flat ground with no screen open. To reopen a block placed earlier:
  `use_at(its coordinates)` with a NON-placeable item selected (your pickaxe) --
  right-clicking with a block in hand places the block instead.
- `furnace_load(item="iron_ore", n=0, fuel="auto")` fills the open furnace (n=0 = the
  whole stack; auto fuel = coal > charcoal > planks > logs > sticks) and does NOT wait;
  `furnace_take()` collects the output once ~200 ticks per item have passed, and refuses
  -- without clicking -- while the output cell is visibly empty.
- `mine_until(item="flint")` holds attack on the aimed block until that item lands.
Every macro starts with a gate (the right screen is open, the recipe's cells are empty)
and ends with a check; on failure it drops the rest of the plan and its [NOTE] names the
fix -- usually `stow_items` for leftovers in the grid, or reopening the screen. Do not
hand-roll a recipe with cursor_to_slot / gui_click when `craft` can do it; the primitives
below exist for RECOVERY (a stack stuck on the cursor, leftovers in a cell, an unusual
container) and for what no macro covers yet.

**The harness measures the cursor for you.** Every turn you are given a line like

    [CURSOR] container=(112.4, 61.0)px  over=inventory slot 12  off-inventory (in the
    cursor or in a crafting grid): oak_planks x4

That position is **measured from the frame** -- the rendered pointer is located in every
GUI tick's image -- so you never need to track or visually re-check the cursor. Trust
`over=` over your own read of the picture. The primitives are closed loop:
1. `cursor_to_slot(slot=<0-35>)` LANDS the cursor on a player inventory slot (the [INV]
   slot ids; 0-8 is the hotbar, 9-35 the three main rows). `cursor_to_cell(grid="3x3",
   cell=4)` lands it on a crafting cell; `cell="out"` is the output; `grid="furnace"`:
   cell 0 = the smelt input, cell 1 = the fuel slot, `"out"` = the result.
2. `gui_click()` picks up or drops a whole stack; `gui_right_click()` places one item.
3. The [INV] and [EVENT] lines in `logs.txt` are the ground truth
   for what a click did: **no [INV] line and no `craft_item`/`pickup` event means the
   click changed nothing**. The frame is not proof: it lags a tick and does not show what
   the cursor is holding.
4. The **[GRID]** line reads the frame at every grid slot's known position and lists the
   ones that visibly hold an item; read only your open screen's row. Leftovers in cells
   are retrieved with `stow_items(grid=..., cells=[...])` (banks the cursor stack too).

**A close that would drop items is refused.** Closing a screen while something is
off-inventory throws it on the floor -- it cost a previous run four of its five logs -- so
the runner turns that toggle into a no-op and writes a [NOTE]. Put the stack back in a
slot (`stow_items`), then close. If you *mean* to drop it, `{"procedure":
"close_inventory", "args": {"force": true}}`. A furnace KEEPS its cells across a close.

**Do not move while a table/furnace screen is open.** The game itself closes the screen
when you walk out of range (~5 blocks), and THAT close bypasses the runner's guard --
whatever the cursor held hits the floor. Stand ADJACENT to the block before opening it;
finish the recipe, close, then move.

**A click that worked can still read as no change for a frame.** The GUI applies clicks on
its own tick, so [INV]/[CURSOR] may lag one frame behind a click that in fact landed. On a
no-change reading, read the NEXT frame first; if two re-clicks in a row change nothing, the
state assumption is wrong (screen closed, cursor over the wrong cell) -- verify the open.

**An unplanned held stack gets stowed FIRST.** When [CURSOR] reports the cursor holding
something your current plan did not put there, one left-click on a confirmed-empty
inventory slot banks it (or `stow_items`). Every plan built on top of a surprise held
stack misclicks. A cursor move or click that finds the screen closed, a click whose
pointer is no longer where the last cursor move landed, or a left-click that lifts
nothing drops the rest of the plan with a [NOTE] saying so.

"""lava_ahead: lava in the lower view (1.5% below y 40 or in the Nether, 4% above) while a walk or a dig moves you, or at a look -- stop; in it, climb out. Flames are not lava."""
# Example reflex (harness-written, yours to edit or retire): the runs that died in lava
# were all MOVING toward it -- a go_to, a mine_ahead, a raw walk -- with the orange already
# in the frame, or stepped into a pool the camera had never looked at (a tunnel whose
# floor was missing). Three cases:

#                                      (strip_segment looks at the next floor before each
#                                      step); a look with nothing queued after it is quiet
#   in the lava (lava damage with   -> stop and climb: back and jump; place a block under
#   the screen orange)                 you if you carry one
# Standing at a pool or a fire on purpose (fill_bucket, use_at, use_held, place_at) is
# exempt: the plan is there by design. A walk covers ~0.9 blocks between two samples, so
# the threshold is low where lava is close (underground, the Nether): a pool three blocks
# ahead reads 2-3% of the lower view; the surface threshold is higher so a distant lake
# does not stop every walk.
# FLAMES ARE NOT LAVA. A fire block (a portal just lit, a burning tree) and the flames
# drawn over the view while you burn share lava's orange, but they are brighter and
# yellower: `fire_frac` runs 5-15x `lava_frac` on flames and 0.3-0.5x on a lake. One life
# lit its portal from inside and this reflex's old in-lava escape pulled it back into the
# fire, where it died with the frame half built; another, burning on a bank, had every
# walk stopped. So flames are left to the plan (walk out, pour water), and the escape
# runs on lava's DAMAGE: lava takes 4 health every 10 ticks, fire 1 every 20, so between
# two samples (4 ticks) only lava takes 3 or more.
# BURNING BESIDE LAVA is the case the colours cannot settle: the overlay over a pool reads
# 1.5-2.5x (two lives burned to death 35 blocks from a stronghold while this reflex took
# the overlay for lava ahead, stepped one back into the pocket and stopped the other's
# climb out, 65 samples in all), and a pool one block away with no fire reads 1.0-1.3x.
# What does settle it is that you are being hurt: flames on screen and health lost in the
# last 100 ticks (`hurt_100`) is a burn, and the plan that is walking out of it is left
# to run. Unhurt, the same picture still stops you.
import json, math, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
MOVING = {"go_to", "mine_ahead", "collect_drops", "raw"}
LOOKING = {"look_abs", "look", "look_at", "watch"}
ON_PURPOSE = {"fill_bucket", "use_at", "use_held", "place_at"}
p, q = s.get("pos"), s.get("pos_prev")
moved = math.hypot(p["x"] - q["x"], p["z"] - q["z"]) if p and q else 0.0
deep = bool(p) and (p["y"] < 40.0 or s.get("dimension") == "the Nether")
thr = 0.015 if deep else 0.04
frac, fire = s["lava_frac"], s.get("fire_frac", 0.0)
entry = s.get("atom") or s.get("entry")      # the atom inside an own procedure
lost = s.get("health_prev", 20) - s.get("health", 20)
flames = fire >= 0.12 and fire > 2.0 * frac      # the overlay flickers down to ~0.14 between flames
burning = fire >= 0.05 and fire > frac and s.get("hurt_100", 0.0) >= 1.0      # 0.06-0.07 between flames
in_lava = bool(s.get("in_lava")) or (lost >= 3.0 and frac >= 0.2)     # head under: the view is flat red, frac ~0
if entry in ON_PURPOSE:
    pass
elif in_lava and p and not s.get("gui_open"):
    block = next((h for h in s.get("hotbar", []) if h.get("item") in ("cobblestone", "dirt", "netherrack", "stone", "gravel")), None)
    acts = ([{"procedure": "equip_hotbar", "args": {"slot": int(block["slot"]) + 1}}] if block else []) +            [{"action": {"back": 1, "jump": 1, **({"use": 1} if block else {})}, "repeat": 10}]
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "IN LAVA at (%.0f, %.1f, %.0f), health %.0f: climbing out -- back and jump%s. "
                              "Then seal the pool with blocks before any step toward it"
                              % (p["x"], p["y"], p["z"], s.get("health", 0), " placing %s under you" % block["item"] if block else ""),
                      "actions": acts}))
elif flames or burning:
    pass          # a fire block or the burning overlay: the plan walks out of it or pours water
elif frac >= thr and entry in MOVING and (moved >= 0.1 or entry == "mine_ahead"):
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "lava fills %d%% of the lower view during %s -- stopped holding sneak; inspect the ledge before moving; "
                              "seal the flow with a block or go around, never through"
                              % (round(100 * frac), entry),
                      "actions": [{"action": {"sneak": 1}, "repeat": 6}]}))
elif frac >= thr and entry in LOOKING and s.get("queue_len", 0) > 1:      # something queued after the look
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "lava fills %d%% of the lower view at a %s -- the plan was about to step there; "
                              "stopped before the step. Seal it (place_at cobblestone on the lava) or turn"
                              % (round(100 * frac), entry)}))

#!<path>
"""Crop a frame region and magnify it, for reading detail a full frame hides.

    ./tools/zoom.py <frame.png> <x> <y> <w> <h> [out.png]

x,y = top-left of the region in the frame's own pixels (640x360); the crop is scaled
4x nearest-neighbour (pixel-accurate, no smoothing) into out.png (default ./zoom.png).
Then open the result with view_image. Compare two frames by zooming the same region in
both and viewing them in sequence.
"""
import sys
from PIL import Image

frame, x, y, w, h = sys.argv[1], *map(int, sys.argv[2:6])
out = sys.argv[6] if len(sys.argv) > 6 else "zoom.png"
img = Image.open(frame).convert("RGB")
x = max(0, min(img.width - 1, x)); y = max(0, min(img.height - 1, y))
w = max(1, min(img.width - x, w)); h = max(1, min(img.height - y, h))
img.crop((x, y, x + w, y + h)).resize((w * 4, h * 4), Image.NEAREST).save(out)
print(f"wrote {out}: {w}x{h} region at ({x},{y}), 4x")

"""aim_speckles: turn the crosshair onto the (x, y) pixel a 'mining stopped: ...-ore-like speckles' [NOTE] names, then mine that block and sweep its drop."""
# Example procedure (harness-written; copy it to mine/procedures/ and make it yours).
# Why it exists: the life that found the diamond did exactly this within 20 steps of the
# watcher's [NOTE] -- aim at the speckles, mine the block under the crosshair, walk to the
# drop. Lives that answered a sighting with "finish the column first" or "craft a sword
# first" never mined the ore at all: by the next turn the view had moved and the speckles
# were gone. So: a sighting [NOTE] outranks everything; call this from its (x, y) BEFORE any
# other look or step, while the view is still the flag-time view (the runner dropped the
# rest of the plan for exactly that).
# The frame the watcher reads is 640x360 with a 70-degree vertical field of view: the focal
# length is 180 / tan(35 deg) = 257 px, so an offset of d pixels from the centre (320, 180) is
# atan(d / 257) degrees -- 104 px right is 22 degrees of yaw, not the 17 a linear scale gives.
# Two 30-tick holds: ore takes longer than stone, and the hold is cut the moment the block
# breaks anyway. collect_drops then sweeps the drop; the milestone is the PICKUP, not the break.
import json, math, sys
PARAMS = {"x": "screen x from the [NOTE] (0-640)", "y": "screen y from the [NOTE] (0-360)",
          "pick": "hotbar slot 1-9 with the pickaxe (default: the best in the hotbar)"}
args = json.loads(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--args") + 1]) if "--args" in sys.argv else {}
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
if s.get("gui_open"):
    raise SystemExit("a screen is open: close_inventory first")
if "x" not in args or "y" not in args:
    raise SystemExit("pass x and y: the pixel the sighting [NOTE] names, e.g. (424, 145)")
x, y = float(args["x"]), float(args["y"])
if not (0 <= x <= 640 and 0 <= y <= 360):
    raise SystemExit("x must be 0-640 and y 0-360 (the [NOTE]'s frame)")
rank = {"diamond_pickaxe": 0, "iron_pickaxe": 1, "stone_pickaxe": 2, "wooden_pickaxe": 3}
picks = [h for h in s["hotbar"] if h.get("item") in rank]
if args.get("pick") is not None:
    picks = [h for h in picks if int(h["slot"]) + 1 == int(args["pick"])]
if not picks:
    raise SystemExit("no pickaxe in the hotbar (diamond ore needs IRON or better to drop a diamond)")
pick = min(picks, key=lambda h: rank[h["item"]])
F = 180.0 / math.tan(math.radians(35.0))               # 257 px
dpitch = round(math.degrees(math.atan((y - 180.0) / F)), 1)   # + is down, like the screen
dyaw = round(math.degrees(math.atan((x - 320.0) / F)), 1)     # + is right, like the screen
plan = [{"procedure": "equip_hotbar", "args": {"slot": int(pick["slot"]) + 1}},
        {"action": {"camera": [dpitch, dyaw]}, "repeat": 1},
        {"action": {"attack": 1}, "repeat": 30},
        {"action": {"attack": 1}, "repeat": 30},
        {"procedure": "collect_drops", "args": {"ticks": 48}}]
print(json.dumps({"actions": plan}))

"""fell: 2+ blocks down within four ticks (a free fall of 3+) -- a drop the plan did not see; stop and look."""
# Example reflex: a hole under a walk, a ledge, a shaft. The plan that fell is wrong
# about the ground; the next move must come from a look, not from the rest of it. A
# walked staircase never drops more than a block in four ticks; free fall does after
# ~9 ticks (3+ blocks), whichever four-tick window the sample lands in.
import json, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
p, q = s.get("pos"), s.get("pos_prev")
if p and q and q["y"] - p["y"] >= 2.0:
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "dropping %.1f blocks in four ticks, a fall, now at (%.0f, %.0f, %.0f) -- "
                              "look at four yaws before moving; go back up the way you came "
                              "(pillar_up, a stair), never onward"
                              % (q["y"] - p["y"], p["x"], p["y"], p["z"])}))

"""hit: 3+ health lost in four ticks with no lava or flames in view -- a mob; stop, decide, act."""
# Example reflex: monsters are reported on no channel; the health drop is the only sign.
# A plan standing still under hits (a dig, a sweep, a click) is how most deaths began.
# The stop hands you the turn at zero game-clock cost: wall the tunnel (place_at), pillar
# up two blocks (pillar_up), or fight with the sword selected -- your call, made now.
# With a block in the hotbar it pillars up two blocks at once (pillar_up, an atom): most
# mobs cannot reach you there, and the turn is yours to wall off or fight. Not during a
# place_at or a use_at: the pillar swaps the hand to the block and leaves a column in
# the middle of what you were building (a portal frame, a wall).
import json, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
lost = s.get("health_prev", s["health"]) - s["health"]
if lost >= 3.0 and s["lava_frac"] < 0.01 and s.get("fire_frac", 0.0) < 0.2 and not s.get("in_lava"):
    block = next((h for h in s.get("hotbar", []) if h.get("item") in ("cobblestone", "dirt", "netherrack", "stone", "gravel")), None)
    pillar = bool(block) and not s.get("gui_open") and (s.get("atom") or s.get("entry")) not in ("pillar_up", "place_at", "use_at")
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "took %.0f damage (health %.0f/20) with no lava in view: a mob is at you. "
                              "Do not keep digging or clicking -- %s"
                              % (lost, s["health"], "pillared up 2 blocks; wall off or fight from there" if pillar
                                 else "wall off, pillar up, or fight now"),
                      **({"actions": [{"procedure": "pillar_up", "args": {"n": 2}}]} if pillar else {})}))

"""lava_ahead: lava in the lower view (1.5% below y 40 or in the Nether, 4% above) while a walk or a dig moves you, or at a look -- stop; in it, climb out. Flames are not lava."""
# Example reflex (harness-written, yours to edit or retire): the runs that died in lava
# were all MOVING toward it -- a go_to, a mine_ahead, a raw walk -- with the orange already
# in the frame, or stepped into a pool the camera had never looked at (a tunnel whose
# floor was missing). Three cases:
#   moving with lava in view        -> stop and hold sneak; inspect footing
#   a look_abs/watch shows lava     -> stop, no step: the plan was about to walk there
#                                      (strip_segment looks at the next floor before each
#                                      step); a look with nothing queued after it is quiet
#   in the lava (lava damage with   -> stop and climb: back and jump; place a block under
#   the screen orange)                 you if you carry one
# Standing at a pool or a fire on purpose (fill_bucket, use_at, use_held, place_at) is
# exempt: the plan is there by design. A walk covers ~0.9 blocks between two samples, so
# the threshold is low where lava is close (underground, the Nether): a pool three blocks
# ahead reads 2-3% of the lower view; the surface threshold is higher so a distant lake
# does not stop every walk.
# FLAMES ARE NOT LAVA. A fire block (a portal just lit, a burning tree) and the flames
# drawn over the view while you burn share lava's orange, but they are brighter and
# yellower: `fire_frac` runs 5-15x `lava_frac` on flames and 0.3-0.5x on a lake. One life
# lit its portal from inside and this reflex's old in-lava escape pulled it back into the
# fire, where it died with the frame half built; another, burning on a bank, had every
# walk stopped. So flames are left to the plan (walk out, pour water), and the escape
# runs on lava's DAMAGE: lava takes 4 health every 10 ticks, fire 1 every 20, so between
# two samples (4 ticks) only lava takes 3 or more.
# BURNING BESIDE LAVA is the case the colours cannot settle: the overlay over a pool reads
# 1.5-2.5x (two lives burned to death 35 blocks from a stronghold while this reflex took
# the overlay for lava ahead, stepped one back into the pocket and stopped the other's
# climb out, 65 samples in all), and a pool one block away with no fire reads 1.0-1.3x.
# What does settle it is that you are being hurt: flames on screen and health lost in the
# last 100 ticks (`hurt_100`) is a burn, and the plan that is walking out of it is left
# to run. Unhurt, the same picture still stops you.
import json, math, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
MOVING = {"go_to", "mine_ahead", "collect_drops", "raw"}
LOOKING = {"look_abs", "look", "look_at", "watch"}
ON_PURPOSE = {"fill_bucket", "use_at", "use_held", "place_at"}
p, q = s.get("pos"), s.get("pos_prev")
moved = math.hypot(p["x"] - q["x"], p["z"] - q["z"]) if p and q else 0.0
deep = bool(p) and (p["y"] < 40.0 or s.get("dimension") == "the Nether")
thr = 0.015 if deep else 0.04
frac, fire = s["lava_frac"], s.get("fire_frac", 0.0)
entry = s.get("atom") or s.get("entry")      # the atom inside an own procedure
lost = s.get("health_prev", 20) - s.get("health", 20)
flames = fire >= 0.12 and fire > 2.0 * frac      # the overlay flickers down to ~0.14 between flames
burning = fire >= 0.05 and fire > frac and s.get("hurt_100", 0.0) >= 1.0      # 0.06-0.07 between flames
in_lava = bool(s.get("in_lava")) or (lost >= 3.0 and frac >= 0.2)     # head under: the view is flat red, frac ~0
if entry in ON_PURPOSE:
    pass
elif in_lava and p and not s.get("gui_open"):
    block = next((h for h in s.get("hotbar", []) if h.get("item") in ("cobblestone", "dirt", "netherrack", "stone", "gravel")), None)
    acts = ([{"procedure": "equip_hotbar", "args": {"slot": int(block["slot"]) + 1}}] if block else []) +            [{"action": {"back": 1, "jump": 1, **({"use": 1} if block else {})}, "repeat": 10}]
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "IN LAVA at (%.0f, %.1f, %.0f), health %.0f: climbing out -- back and jump%s. "
                              "Then seal the pool with blocks before any step toward it"
                              % (p["x"], p["y"], p["z"], s.get("health", 0), " placing %s under you" % block["item"] if block else ""),
                      "actions": acts}))
elif flames or burning:
    pass          # a fire block or the burning overlay: the plan walks out of it or pours water
elif frac >= thr and entry in MOVING and (moved >= 0.1 or entry == "mine_ahead"):
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "lava fills %d%% of the lower view during %s -- stopped holding sneak; inspect the ledge before moving; "
                              "seal the flow with a block or go around, never through"
                              % (round(100 * frac), entry),
                      "actions": [{"action": {"sneak": 1}, "repeat": 6}]}))
elif frac >= thr and entry in LOOKING and s.get("queue_len", 0) > 1:      # something queued after the look
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "lava fills %d%% of the lower view at a %s -- the plan was about to step there; "
                              "stopped before the step. Seal it (place_at cobblestone on the lava) or turn"
                              % (round(100 * frac), entry)}))

"""starving: the food bar below 18 -- no natural healing from here; eats what you carry, else a note."""
# Example reflex: health regenerates only with the food bar at 18+, and this engine drains
# about one point per 4000 steps, so a life that never eats spends its second half unable
# to heal. Fires only when the bar has just dropped a point: with food carried it runs `eat`
# (one turn); with none it notes the crossing below 18 once; at health 10.5 with nothing to
# eat it stops the plan once. Never every tick.
import json, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
f, fp = s.get("food", 20), s.get("food_prev", 20)
h, hp = s.get("health", 20), s.get("health_prev", 20)
FOODS = ("cooked_beef", "cooked_porkchop", "cooked_mutton", "cooked_chicken", "steak",
         "golden_apple", "bread", "cooked_cod", "cooked_salmon", "baked_potato", "apple",
         "carrot", "melon_slice", "cookie", "beef", "porkchop", "mutton", "chicken",
         "potato", "beetroot", "sweet_berries")
inv = s.get("inventory") or {}
food = next((k for k in FOODS if inv.get(k, 0) > 0), None)
if f < 18 and f < fp and food and not s.get("gui_open") and (s.get("atom") or s.get("entry")) != "eat":
    print(json.dumps({"actions": [{"procedure": "eat", "args": {"item": food}}],
                      "note": "food %.0f/20 with %s carried: eating (no natural healing below 18)"
                              % (f, food)}))
elif f < 18 and fp >= 18 and (s.get("atom") or s.get("entry")) != "eat":
    print(json.dumps({"note": ("food %.0f/20: no natural healing from here; eat the %s once the GUI is closed"
                               % (f, food)) if food else
                              ("food %.0f/20 and nothing to eat: no natural healing from here. "
                               "Any animal in view is one kill of food" % f)}))
elif h <= 10.5 and hp > 10.5 and f < 18 and not food:
    print(json.dumps({"stop": True,
                      "note": "health %.0f/20, food %.0f/20, nothing to eat: you cannot heal until "
                              "you eat" % (h, f)}))
